Office Visit - Follow-up
Patient: Dario Castellano | DOB: 12/24/1981 | MRN: SYN-4797756
Date of service: 08/27/2025 | Dr. Adele Cordero, MD

History of present illness:
43-year-old man seen for follow-up of low back pain. Low back pain radiating to the right leg for 17 weeks.

Treatment to date:
Completed 9 weeks of physical therapy and daily naproxen without adequate relief.

History:
Past medical history: hyperlipidemia, seasonal allergies.
Medications: atorvastatin 20 mg nightly; loratadine 10 mg daily.

Review of systems:
Red flag screen negative: denies bowel or bladder dysfunction, saddle anesthesia, fever, unexplained weight loss, or history of cancer.

Physical exam:
Back: tenderness over the lower lumbar paraspinal muscles; straight-leg raise positive on the right at 30 degrees.
Neuro: strength 4/5 in right ankle dorsiflexion and great toe extension, reflexes 2+ and symmetric, decreased light touch over the dorsum of the right foot.

Assessment and plan:
Assessment: right L5 lumbar radiculopathy.
Plan: MRI lumbar spine without contrast to evaluate for disc herniation; home exercise program; follow up after imaging.
